Children wait outside of an immigration court at the Jacob K. Javits Federal Building on July 31, 2026 in New York City.
                
                    
                    Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images North America

August 1, 2026 • Thousands of unaccompanied immigrant children are set to lose legal representation. The federal contract that pays for legal access expired Friday.

Asylum seekers queue at the entrance of Mexico's Refugee Help Commission and UNHCR offices in Tijuana, Mexico on January 24, 2025.
                
                    
                    Guillermo Arias/AFP via Getty Images
                    
                
                hide caption

July 30, 2026 • A new rule for asylum applications adds to the bevy of changes under the Trump administration to the core program for those fleeing persecution in their home countries.

Federal immigration officers can be heard using slurs during a raid in Los Angeles County last year, in bodycam footage obtained by the ACLU and submitted as evidence in a federal lawsuit.
                
                    
                    Department of Homeland Security/Screenshot by NPR
                    
                
                hide caption

July 29, 2026 • In its lawsuit alleging racial profiling, the ACLU uncovered bodycam footage and texts in which immigration agents used slurs to describe Latinos targeted in Los Angeles raids last year.

Farah Larrieux stands in her backyard in South Florida on July 27.
                
                    
                    Reshma Kirpalani for NPR/‎
                    
                
                hide caption

July 29, 2026 • Temporary protected status was given to Haitians after the 2010 quake because Haiti was deemed too dangerous for a safe return. In June, the Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to end TPS.

Members of the National Guard stand watch on Beale St., Friday, July 17, 2026, in Memphis, Tenn.
                
                    
                    George Walker IV/AP
                    
                
                hide caption

July 27, 2026 • The influx of federal agents into the city last fall led to widespread immigration arrests – a majority without criminal convictions. President Trump has said he wants to replicate it elsewhere.

Some 350,000 Haitian migrants are set to lose their temporary legal status next week. Many have had children in the U.S., and now face an agonizing choice: if deported, should they take their U.S. citizen children to a still-dangerous Haiti? Families at this Haitian church in San Diego are leaning on faith as they brace for an uncertain future.
                
                    
                    Adrian Florido/NPR
                    
                
                hide caption

July 23, 2026 • A Supreme Court ruling stripped Haitian migrants of their temporary legal status. Those with U.S.-born children face an agonizing choice if deported: Should they take them to a still-dangerous Haiti?

An FBI official places an evidence card in Biddeford where a man was killed in a shooting involving U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents on July 13, 2026.
                
                    
                    Gregory Rec/Portland Press Herald
                    
                
                hide caption

July 23, 2026 • The recent fatal shootings by ICE officers in Texas and Maine come at a time when the federal agency has hired a huge number of officers quickly. Some law enforcement experts worry that this kind of a hiring spree can lead police agencies to cut corners in vetting new hires.

Rachel Reyes holds a photo of her son, Ruben Ray Martinez, a U.S. citizen who was shot and killed by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent during a traffic encounter in Texas.
                
                    
                    Brenda Bazán for NPR
                    
                
                hide caption

July 22, 2026 • Ruben Ray Martinez, 23, was fatally shot by an ICE agent two months into President Trump's second term. His mother says her family has yet to receive justice.

Children in Asian Refugees United's Soccer for Success program huddle during soccer practice in Harrisburg, Pa., on April 16, 2025.
                
                    
                    Maansi Srivastava/NPR
                    
                
                hide caption

July 21, 2026 • Harrisburg is home to one of the nation's largest communities of Nepali-speaking Bhutanese refugees and their families. Through soccer, generations have found connection, belonging and a way to carry forward a shared history.

July 20, 2026 • International students could once stay as long as they needed to complete their college degrees, but that's changing, and the restrictions could cut into college budgets.

A federal agent wears an Immigration and Customs Enforcement badge in New York, June 10, 2025. The ICE officer who allegedly fatally shot a Colombian man in Maine on Monday was prone to violence and held racist beliefs, according to some of the people who were close to him.
                
                    
                    Yuki Iwamura/AP
                    
                
                hide caption

July 17, 2026 • Ashley Brouillette has identified her ex-husband, David Brouillette, as the officer who fatally shot Joan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Biddeford, Maine, on Monday. She said she learned he was the officer responsible when he called her on Wednesday.

Demonstrators wave flags at a rally in support of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) at the State House in Augusta, Maine, on July 15.
                
                    
                    Joseph Prezioso/AFP via Getty Images
                    
                
                hide caption

July 17, 2026 • Republicans are spending more money and running more ads on immigration than Democrats are ahead of the November midterm elections, according to an NPR analysis of advertisement data.

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt speaks during a press briefing in the Brady Briefing Room of the White House in Washington, DC, on July 16, 2026.
                
                    
                    Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images
                    
                
                hide caption

July 16, 2026 • The comments came following widespread reports earlier in the week that those stops would be put on pause after two immigrants were fatally shot by ICE agents in early July.

Federal law enforcement agents confront demonstrators protesting outside an immigration processing center on Sept. 19, 2025, in Broadview, Ill. The demonstrators were protesting a recent surge in ICE activity in the Chicago area, part of the Trump administration's crackdown on undocumented immigrants in the area dubbed Operation Midway Blitz.
                
                    
                    Scott Olson/Getty Images
                    
                
                hide caption

July 16, 2026 • An ACLU report looks at widespread use of force in immigration enforcement in the first year of President Trump's return to office. Recent fatal shootings in Texas and Maine have renewed scrutiny on the agency's tactics.

A federal agent wears a body camera as they patrol the halls of immigration court at the Jacob K. Javits Federal Building on March 04, 2026 in New York City.
                
                    
                    Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images North America
                    
                
                hide caption

July 16, 2026 • In recent days, federal immigration agents fatally shot two immigrant fathers. None of the federal officers involved were wearing body cameras, the agency said.

Family members of Mexican immigrant Lorenzo Salgado Araujo grieve at a makeshift memorial during a candlelight vigil on July 08, 2026 in Houston, Texas. An Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer fatally shot Mexican immigrant Lorenzo Salgado Araujo during an attempted traffic stop arrest on Tuesday.
                
                    
                    Brandon Bell/Getty Images
                    
                
                hide caption

July 14, 2026 • There have been at least 9 deaths tied to immigration enforcement actions since President Trump returned to the White House. Four of them have been this year.

FBI investigators work the scene of an alleged ICE involved shooting in Biddeford, Maine, on July 13, 2026.
                
                    
                    Joseph Prezioso/AFP via Getty Images
                    
                
                hide caption

July 14, 2026 • U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement will pause non-urgent vehicle stops after two deadly shootings in less than a week, Maine U.S. Sen. Angus King's office tells NPR.

Mourners, including María Guadalupe Rodríguez (kneeling), pray and pay their respects in front of a makeshift memorial for Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a Mexican immigrant shot and killed by immigration agents in Houston.
                
                    
                    Sergio Martínez-Beltrán/NPR
                    
                
                hide caption

July 10, 2026 • Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was a 52-year-old Mexican national who worked in construction for more than three decades. The father of three was shot by Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents after they attempted to pull him over.

Farmworkers harvest strawberries in a field on Farmworkers Day on March 31 near Oxnard, Calif.
                
                    
                    Mario Tama/Getty Images
                    
                
                hide caption

July 10, 2026 • Republicans on Capitol Hill are starting to talk about one facet of immigration reform: how to expand the popular H-2A visa program for farm laborers. They face obstacles.

People wave U.S. flags to celebrate becoming U.S. citizens after taking the oath of allegiance during a naturalization ceremony in Boston in January 2025.
                
                    
                    Joseph Prezioso/AFP via Getty Images
                    
                
                hide caption

July 6, 2026 • Spouses of U.S. citizens have traditionally had a special place in immigration law. That's no longer the case, according to the administration and immigration lawyers.

Healthcare workers rally at a Manhattan union headquarters to show support for the Haitian and Syrian communities after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that the Trump administration could end temporary protected status for potentially millions of foreign nationals from countries experiencing conflict and violence. The decision means that over 330,000 Haitians and Syrians could lose their work authorizations and ability to remain in the country.
                
                    
                    Spencer Platt/Getty Images
                    
                
                hide caption

July 2, 2026 • Mass deportations would be felt across hospitals and emergency rooms, which already face persistent staffing shortfalls. The long-term healthcare sector will suffer the greatest disruptions, experts say.

June 30, 2026 • As the Supreme Court today weighs the Trump administration's effort to revoke birthright citizenship, NPR looks at what else the White House has done to curb illegal and legal migration.

Mexican Army rescue workers search Sunday for people trapped in collapsed buildings after earthquakes struck La Guaira, Venezuela.
                
                    
                    Matias Delacroix/AP
                    
                
                hide caption

June 30, 2026 • On June 24, 146 Venezuelans were deported from Texas to Caracas. Hours later, while the deportees were in a guarded hotel, powerful twin earthquakes struck.

June 30, 2026 • Hundreds of people detained at an ICE detention center in Newark, NJ refused to eat and work for a month. They were protesting the conditions inside — spoiled food, lack of medical care, overcrowding. The detainees are the ones who actually keep the facility running — cooking, cleaning, doing laundry — all while getting paid a dollar a day. This week, two reporters who have been covering the strikes, José Olivares and Sophie Hurwitz, talk about what happens when detainees stop eating and working — and what it means that the government insists none of it is happening.
